title: Tenali and the Envious Courtiers' Thorn Trap
summary: Three senior ministers of Vijayanagara, consumed by jealousy over King Krishnadevaraya’s high regard for Tenali Raman, hatched a petty plot to humiliate him during the royal Diw...
full_text:
Three senior ministers of Vijayanagara, consumed by jealousy over King Krishnadevaraya’s high regard for Tenali Raman, hatched a petty plot to humiliate him during the royal Diwali celebrations.

Before the court assembled, they secretly scattered long, sharp *babul* acacia thorns across the cushions of Tenali’s customary silk seat in the second row of the audience hall, covering them with a thin layer of rose petals so the trap was invisible.
They whispered: 'When the jester sits, he will scream like a stuck pig, jump in the air, and disgrace himself before the Emperor!'

Tenali Raman entered the hall, dressed in festive white silks. As he approached his seat, his sharp eyes noticed two thorns poking through the rose petals and caught the guilty, expectant smirks on the three ministers' faces.

Instead of sitting immediately, Tenali bowed with immense grace to the three plotters. He then carefully placed his heavy palm-leaf manuscript upon the cushion to flatten the thorns safely, and sat down gently with complete composure.
He closed his eyes and exclaimed in a loud voice of ecstasy:
'Aha! Ah! What exquisite heavenly bliss! What transcendent fragrance!'

King Krishnadevaraya looked over from his throne, curious:
'Tenali, what brings such sudden ecstasy to thy countenance?'

Tenali stood up, holding a handful of the rose petals mixed with the acacia thorns, and proclaimed:
'Jahanpanah! Look at the noble generosity of my dear ministerial colleagues!
Knowing that a courtier's mind must remain sharp and vigilant, they have arranged a sublime spiritual seat for me! The fragrant rose petals symbolize the Emperor's loving grace, while these sharp thorns symbolize the rigorous vigilance required to defend our borders!
They honored me with this special seat of wisdom!'

The King was deeply touched by what he assumed was a profound philosophical gesture by the ministers:
'Marvelous! What noble fraternal affection!
Since these three ministers conceived such a sublime spiritual seat, it is only fitting that they receive the highest honor of their own invention!'

The King commanded the royal guards:
'Bring three large sacks of fresh babul acacia thorns! Scatter them thickly across the velvet thrones of these three noble ministers, and let them sit upon them for the remainder of today’s four-hour assembly to share Tenali’s spiritual bliss!'

The three ministers turned green with horror. Under the Emperor’s watchful eyes, they were forced to sit on their thorn-covered cushions, squirming, grimacing in agony, their teeth clenched, unable to cry out lest they offend the King!

Tenali smiled cheerfully from his safe seat, proving that those who dig pits of malice inevitably tumble into their own traps.
moral: Those who plant thorns for others find their own schemes transformed into blessings for the righteous.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tenali and the Envious Courtiers"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
